name: Washed-out destructive buttons
summary: Give destructive actions a solid, readable treatment with a clear verb, not pale red text on a translucent red tint.
problem: Low-contrast tinted ghost buttons fail contrast, look disabled and make the most consequential action the least legible one. They also lean on colour alone to signal danger.

bad.description: A pale red label on a translucent dark red background with a vague "Delete" label.

good.title: Solid destructive button
good.description: Use .btn-danger: solid danger fill, white text, a trash icon and a specific verb ("Delete project").

good.title: Neutral, confirm next
good.description: When the action is not the focus of the view, use a neutral secondary button with the same verb and icon, and put the danger treatment on the confirmation step.

why: A solid fill is readable at a glance and keeps danger distinguishable without relying on hue. A specific verb and icon add non-colour cues.
exceptions: A low-emphasis inline text action (for example "Remove" in a row, or a danger item in a menu) may use the danger text colour on an opaque surface if it meets 4.5:1 contrast and has a clear verb. The prohibited part is the translucent tinted fill with pale text.

humanReview: Is the destructive label readable at a glance and does it name the object being destroyed?
Does a confirmation or undo protect the action?
